title: React Native and Vega OS integration
lead: These two directories provide source code for integration into external native projects. Passing the repository’s type checks and unit tests does not establish that the resulting apps build or play on a device.

blocks.text: React Native and Expo

apps/react-native provides the existing showcase App.tsx, source list, DVR logic, configuration controls, and a generator for an external Expo development project. The generated host pins Node 24.19.0, pnpm 10.33.0, Expo 54.0.35, React Native 0.81.5, React 19.1.0, bitmovin-player-react-native 1.28.0, and the Expo 54-compatible expo-crypto 15.0.9. Its pnpm-lock.yaml preserves the JavaScript dependency resolution.

The wrapper resolves iOS Player and Player Core 3.126.0, Analytics 3.28.1, and Google IMA 3.26.1 through Swift Package Manager; Android Player is 3.165.0+jason. The included native dependency locks preserve the iOS resolution. The standalone iOS 3.128.0 and Android 3.171.0 samples use separate SDK pins; do not force those versions into this wrapper.

The +jason suffix selects Bitmovin's Android build that renames media-library namespaces and resources to avoid conflicts with Media3/ExoPlayer. Google IMA 3.37.0 and later require this build and core-library desugaring, which adapts newer Java library APIs for older Android versions. Wrapper 1.28.0 selects Player and media-session 3.165.0+jason, IMA 3.38.0, and desugar_jdk_libs 2.1.5. Its Expo plugin has no native Player SDK version option. Keep these related dependencies together; changing only the Player version is not a verified wrapper upgrade.

blocks.title: Generate the external host from the repository root
blocks.text:
pnpm --filter @showcase/ui-shared build
bash scripts/sync-env.sh
node apps/react-native/scripts/create-expo-project.mjs ../player-lab-react-native --env-from apps/react-native/.env

The generator uses the native template included in Expo 54 rather than create-expo-app@latest. Its target must be a new directory outside the checkout. It copies the existing App and registers it as the root screen with a safe area. Native Player modules require a development build; Expo Go cannot run them.
The generated app is named Player Lab React Native and uses com.playerlab.reactnative for both iOS and Android. Its app.json registers the Player plugin and the included shared UI asset plugin:

blocks.title: Generated app identifiers and plugins

items: Configure the repository root keys and run the preparation commands above. --env-from explicitly copies the generated ignored apps/react-native/.env with mode 0600; omit it to generate a project without keys. Keys are never inserted into app.json.
Authorize com.playerlab.reactnative on the Player license being used. Optional Analytics has a separate license and authorization. Never commit .env or native build output.

Install the generated pinned dependencies and run Expo prebuild. For iOS, restore the supplied Podfile.lock before pod install, then the supplied workspace Package.resolved before building, using the commands below.

The included plugin copies shared JS/CSS into Android app/src/main/assets/webui and iOS Copy Bundle Resources. App.tsx resolves Android asset URLs and iOS main-bundle filenames directly; no placeholder delivery path remains.

After editing the shared UI, rebuild it, copy its JS/CSS into the external project assets/webui directory, rerun prebuild, and rebuild the native app. A Metro reload alone cannot update native resources.
Run the iOS or Android development build from the external project and check the actual SDK UI, advancing VOD, Apply/Reset, and background/foreground return.

blocks.text: On macOS, use Xcode and CocoaPods for iOS; Android requires Java 17 and the Android SDK/toolchain selected by Expo 54. The supplied Podfile.lock was generated with CocoaPods 1.17.0. Since wrapper 1.27, iOS Player and Google IMA use Swift Package Manager, while the bridge and Expo use CocoaPods. Existing integrations should follow the official migration guide. Keep both Podfile.lock and the workspace Package.resolved; restore the supplied locks after generating a fresh project.

blocks.title: Install, prebuild, and restore iOS dependency locks
blocks.text:
cd ../player-lab-react-native
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
pnpm exec expo prebuild --no-install
cp native-locks/Podfile.lock ios/Podfile.lock
(cd ios && pod install)
mkdir -p ios/PlayerLabReactNative.xcworkspace/xcshareddata/swiftpm
cp native-locks/Package.resolved ios/PlayerLabReactNative.xcworkspace/xcshareddata/swiftpm/Package.resolved

blocks.title: Choose the target command in the external Expo project
blocks.text:
pnpm exec expo run:ios
pnpm exec expo run:android

The screen includes Default, Sports, Live (DVR), and Cinema UI choices; source buttons; Live edge; −10/−30/−60-second controls; Allow DVR; state; an event log; and Show configuration. iOS starts with HLS and offers HLS/progressive MP4; DASH types and presets are hidden there. Android also offers DASH.

Show configuration edits the required HTTP/HTTPS source URL, type, optional title/poster URL, start offset in seconds, and its Start/End/SDK default reference. Signed offsets are allowed: Start refers to the beginning of the media/DVR window, End to the end/live edge. The SDK default is Start for VOD and End for live. Blank title/poster/offset fields remove those optional values.

URL validation uses the locally imported URL from react-native-url-polyfill 4.0.0. Older native global URL implementations leave protocol and hostname unimplemented, which would reject valid sources before loading. The local parser leaves global URL and the SDK media shims unchanged.

Autoplay and Mute on startup apply at player creation. Start offsets and buffer durations accept finite decimal seconds. Blank buffer keeps the SDK default (iOS 0, Android 50); iOS 0 lets the SDK choose a duration. This form requires a positive Android buffer target because zero is not its automatic setting. Maximum bitrate accepts whole bits per second: 1–2,147,483,647 on Android and 1–9,007,199,254,740,991 on iOS; blank means no cap. The native bridge converts bitrate to an integer, Android uses a signed 32-bit value, and JavaScript cannot represent integers above its safe limit exactly. Fractions and out-of-range values are rejected before recreation.

Apply and recreate player validates the whole draft, recreates the player, and reloads the selected source from its start offset. Playback position resets and playback starts according to Autoplay. The complete source, chosen UI, log, and Allow DVR setting are retained. Invalid or unchanged settings do not recreate the player. Reset draft only discards edits; it does not change playback. Preset source buttons still load immediately. Allow DVR remains an application helper rather than an editable SDK playback property.

blocks.title: Check logic and types from the repository root
blocks.text:
pnpm --filter @showcase/react-native test
pnpm --filter @showcase/react-native typecheck

Type checks include the actual App and generated host entry point. App interaction tests use native/player mocks; generator tests separately check source/asset copies, pinned inputs, existing-target rejection, and explicit private environment-file copying. Actual iOS 26.4 simulator checks exercised SDK Default VOD playback, packaged Sports INFO and Play/Pause, Reset/Apply, source/UI/log/Allow DVR retention, and advancing VOD after background/foreground return. iOS and ARM64 Android API 36.1 development builds and packaged asset equality passed. Android licensed playback is not yet qualified. Physical devices, Release archives, DRM, advertisements, every shared factory, and live/DVR behavior remain outside this qualification.
Vega OS and Kepler

Vega OS is separate from Android-based Fire TV. The included apps/vega host connects the modular Web Player to W3C Media and retains the existing React Native/Kepler controls. It does not use the browser-based bitmovin-player-ui. The tested combination is Player 8.138.0-beta.28, React Native 0.72.0, React 18.2.0, Kepler 2.1.0+rn0.72.0 and W3C Media 2.3.2, with Vega SDK 0.24.12112 and Kepler CLI platform 0.22.14. The official Vega sample supports the beta.XX channel; the general Web stable release is not a supported substitute.

items: Install the official Vega SDK and documented prerequisites. Normal JavaScript installation, unit tests and type checks do not require the native SDK or a license.
Use the included application host. Generate its ignored runtime configuration before bundling; the build-only example below omits credentials.

For licensed playback, load the repository-root .env with scripts/env-lib.sh and rerun runtime:config before rebuilding. It copies only the Player and optional Analytics licenses; index.js installs them before evaluating App. Authorize com.showcase.dvr.vega on the Player license. Keep generated configuration, bundles, packages and logs private.
Run build:vega through the Vega SDK environment. It creates JS/Hermes bundles and aarch64, armv7 and x86_64 Release packages. The generic workspace build does not run the native SDK.

Start a Vega Virtual Device or connect a compatible device, verify its OS/profile, select its serial explicitly and launch the matching package. Check changing video frames and advancing SDK position together; a CLI ready message alone does not prove that the OS or app booted.

blocks.title: Build without including license credentials
blocks.text:
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
pnpm --filter @showcase/vega runtime:config --without-credentials
vega exec pnpm --filter @showcase/vega build:vega

blocks.title: Inspect and run on a Vega Virtual Device
blocks.text:
vega virtual-device start --timeout 120
vega exec vda devices -l
vega device info --device <VVD_SERIAL>
vega run-app apps/vega/build/aarch64-release/vega_aarch64.vpkg \
  com.showcase.dvr.vega.main --deviceId <VVD_SERIAL>

The screen includes source selection, Live edge, −10/−30/−60-second controls, Allow DVR, state, logs, and Show configuration. Autoplay and mute are initially enabled. It does not provide dedicated play/pause buttons, audio/subtitle/quality selection, or TV remote key-event handling. DRM modules are also excluded.

Show configuration edits an HTTP/HTTPS source URL, HLS/DASH/progressive MP4 type, optional title/poster URL, signed start offset in seconds and Start/End/SDK default reference. Start means beginning of media/DVR window, End means end/live edge; the SDK default is Start for VOD and End for live. Blank title/poster/offset fields remove those optional values. The Kepler screen has no artwork overlay, so a poster value is stored with the source without adding a visible poster.

URL validation uses a local import from react-native-url-polyfill 4.0.0 because React Native 0.72 does not implement all global URL getters. The native global URL and media object URLs are preserved. The dependency is already declared in apps/vega/package.json.

Autoplay and Mute on startup apply at player creation. Separate audio/video forward buffer targets are in seconds; this form accepts positive values, and blank keeps the SDK default of 40 seconds per media type. Live windows can limit the effective buffer. Maximum video bitrate is a positive adaptation cap in bits per second; blank means no cap. Numbers must be finite decimals. Format, buffering and adaptation support still depends on the stream, engine and target device.

Apply and recreate player validates the draft, waits for the previous player to close, and reloads the selected source from its start offset. Playback position resets and playback starts according to Autoplay; the selected/custom source, log and Allow DVR setting are retained. Invalid or unchanged settings do not recreate the player. Reset draft only discards edits. Preset source buttons still load immediately. The HTML Player UI remains disabled on Vega; Allow DVR controls an application helper.

Vega requires native playback resources to be released before background handling yields because its JavaScript thread can be suspended. The AppState handler cancels callbacks, requests synchronous native release and removes the video surface. Ordinary foreground Apply waits for the SDK's asynchronous stop to finish before releasing native media; that stop sequence still uses the media object. Foreground return waits for a new surface and confirmed prior cleanup. A failed or unconfirmed release keeps the previous owner and blocks replacement. Initialization-abort success alone does not confirm release of a later native allocation. The 1000 ms release deadline is this app's policy. Playback position is not restored.

blocks.title: Check the screen and logic from the repository root
blocks.text:
pnpm --filter @showcase/vega test
pnpm --filter @showcase/vega typecheck

The 2026-10-20 run passed 68 unit tests and the full App type check. The final lifecycle implementation built all three Release packages and was installed on an arm64 Vega Virtual Device. Three valid Apply cycles with video bitrate caps of 2, 3 and 4 Mbit/s each showed changing VOD HLS frames and advancing SDK positions in the same app instance. Earlier native checks also confirmed Live DASH playback, remote focus/scrolling, text entry, zero-bitrate validation and Reset. Unit/session tests still mock native media/player boundaries and provide separate evidence.

Before player construction, the runtime connects the published Amazon media/WebCrypto APIs, @xmldom/xmldom 0.9.12 and base-64 1.0.0. PlayerConfig.network.requestApi is fixed to Fetch as required by the integration; it is a code setting, not a GUI selector. Other supplied network hooks remain. Native media and crypto implementations stay in their installed packages. The state line displays PlayerAPI.getCurrentTime() in seconds; live sources can use an absolute media timeline.

blocks.title: Load local licenses before rebuilding
blocks.text:
source scripts/env-lib.sh
load_env_defaults .env
pnpm --filter @showcase/vega runtime:config
vega exec pnpm --filter @showcase/vega build:vega

In the final background/foreground check, the same app instance retained the unapplied title draft and applied bitrate setting, but video remained black and all five SDK position samples stayed at 57.6 seconds. Playback recovery on foreground return failed this check. Fully terminating and relaunching the app restored VOD progress from 1.6 to 5.5 seconds. Process memory and file-descriptor samples were collected, but they do not establish native media/surface allocation counts or leak freedom. Physical Fire TV, DRM/offline behavior, audio correctness and quantitative buffer/bitrate behavior were not qualified. Virtual-device results do not replace target-device compatibility and performance checks.
